extracted.intended_audience: graduate students, postdoctoral scholars, and early-career academics (particularly those from underrepresented racial and ethnic groups) interested in faculty careers and Ford Foundation Fellowships
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and selection criteria for applicants to the Ford Foundation Fellowships program, describing program goals, applicant qualifications, and the kinds of support fellows received (mentorship, professional development, alumni engagement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase diversity of college and university faculties
rubrics_metrics.description: The Ford Foundation Fellowships were designed to increase the diversity of the nation's college and university faculties by increasing their ethnic and racial diversity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program goal used to shape selection and program activities; applicants and program activities were evaluated against their contribution to increasing ethnic and racial diversity in higher education faculty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximize the educational benefits of diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: A program objective was maximizing the educational benefits of diversity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients and program efforts were expected to promote not just representation but the pedagogical and educational gains that come from diverse faculty and perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase the number of professors who use diversity as a resource
rubrics_metrics.description: One explicit aim was increasing the number of professors who use diversity as a resource for enriching the education of all students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection favored candidates who demonstrated how diversity would be integrated into their teaching and scholarship to benefit all students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrated superior academic achievement
rubrics_metrics.description: Support was provided for individuals who demonstrated superior academic achievement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Academic record and accomplishments were a core selection criterion; applicants were evaluated on evidence of high scholarly performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to a career in teaching and research at the college or university level
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants were expected to have committed to a career in teaching and research at the college or university level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection considered applicants' stated career plans and demonstrated commitment to academic teaching and research careers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promise of future achievement as scholars and teachers
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants needed to have shown promise of future achievement as scholars and teachers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators assessed potential for future scholarly productivity and effective teaching, not just past accomplishments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of diversity as a resource for enriching education
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants were expected to have used or plan to use diversity as a resource for enriching the education of all students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants' statements, plans, or evidence that describe concrete ways diversity will inform pedagogy, mentorship, or scholarship strengthened their fit with the program's goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentorship, professional development, and alumni network support
rubrics_metrics.description: The program included mentorship, professional development, and an expansive network of alumni who enable peer support and community building.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the fellowship model — applicants and fellows would participate in and benefit from mentorship and professional-development activities and sustained alumni engagement; program success included provision of these supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support across multiple stages of an academic career
rubrics_metrics.description: Ford Fellowships spanned multiple stages of an academic career and provided support at different career points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program targeted candidates at various career stages (e.g., predoctoral, postdoctoral, early-career) and evaluated fit relative to the stage-specific aims and supports of the fellowship.
